h1: Miles to Kilometers Converter (+ km to miles)
description: Convert miles to kilometers instantly. 1 mile = 1.609344 km exactly (NIST). Works both ways. Includes reference table for common running, driving, and cycling distances.
answerSnippet: 1 mile = 1.609344 kilometers exactly (defined by NIST/international yard-pound agreement, 1959). To convert miles to km, multiply by 1.609344. To convert km to miles, multiply by 0.621371. A 5-mile run = 8.047 km; a 10K race = 6.214 miles; a marathon (42.195 km) = 26.219 miles.
intro: Miles and kilometers are the two most common units of distance worldwide. The **mile** (mi) is standard in the United States, United Kingdom, and a handful of other countries, while the **kilometer** (km) dominates everywhere else. The exact conversion factor — **1 mile = 1.609344 km** — was fixed permanently by the International Yard and Pound Agreement of 1959 and is maintained by NIST. Use this converter for road-trip planning, race distances, trail running, rental-car navigation, or any cross-border distance comparison. The calculator works in both directions: miles → km and km → miles. It also shows the round-trip total, useful for fuel calculations and training plans.
keyTakeaway: **1 mile = 1.609344 km exactly (NIST); 1 km = 0.621371 mi.** A 5-mile run is 8.047 km; a 10K race is 6.214 miles; a marathon is 26.219 miles (42.195 km).

explanation:
## How the Conversion Works

The factor **1.609344** is an exact, legally-defined constant (not a rounded approximation). It derives from:

> 1 mile = 1,760 yards; 1 yard = 0.9144 m (exact) → 1,760 × 0.9144 = **1,609.344 m = 1.609344 km**

```
Miles → Kilometers:   km = mi × 1.609344
Kilometers → Miles:   mi = km ÷ 1.609344  (= km × 0.621371)
```

---

## Worked Examples

### Example 1 — Road trip planning (mi → km)
A driver plans a 350-mile trip and needs the distance in km for a metric GPS:
> 350 mi × 1.609344 = **563.27 km**

### Example 2 — Trail running (km → mi)
A race is advertised as 32 km. An American runner wants the mileage:
> 32 km ÷ 1.609344 = **19.884 mi**

### Example 3 — Speed conversion (mph → km/h)
Since speed is distance per hour, the same factor applies:
> 75 mph × 1.609344 = **120.70 km/h**

---

## Common Mistakes

1. **Using 1.6 instead of 1.609344** — The 1.6 shortcut introduces a 0.58% error; over 100 miles this is nearly 1 km off.
2. **Confusing statute miles with nautical miles** — 1 nautical mile = 1.852 km, not 1.609344 km. Never apply the road-mile factor to aviation/maritime distances.
3. **Inverting the direction** — When converting km → mi, divide by 1.609344 (do NOT multiply).

faq.a: Exactly **1.609344 kilometers**. This is a fixed, legally-defined value established by the International Yard and Pound Agreement (1959) and used by NIST. It is not a rounded approximation — the six decimal places are exact.
**0.621371 miles** (more precisely, 0.6213711922…). This is simply 1 ÷ 1.609344. For quick mental math, 1 km ≈ 0.6 miles, or about 5/8 of a mile.

faq.q: How do I quickly convert miles to km in my head?
faq.a: Multiply by **1.6** for a fast approximation (0.58% low) or use the Fibonacci trick: miles in Fibonacci sequence ≈ km of the next number. For example, 5 miles ≈ 8 km (5 and 8 are consecutive Fibonacci numbers). For accuracy beyond mental math, use this calculator.

faq.q: How far is a 5K in miles?
faq.a: A 5K (5 kilometers) = **3.107 miles** (5 ÷ 1.609344). A 10K = 6.214 miles. A half marathon (21.0975 km) = 13.109 miles. A full marathon (42.195 km) = 26.219 miles.

faq.q: Does mph to km/h use the same conversion factor?
faq.a: Yes. Because speed is distance per hour and the hour cancels, the same factor applies directly: **km/h = mph × 1.609344**. For example, 60 mph = 96.56 km/h; 100 km/h = 62.14 mph (the European motorway benchmark).

faq.q: What is the difference between a statute mile and a nautical mile?
faq.a: A **statute (land) mile** = 1.609344 km. A **nautical mile** = exactly 1.852 km — about 15% longer. Nautical miles are used in aviation and maritime navigation. Never apply the 1.609344 factor to nautical distances.

faq.q: Why does the US still use miles instead of kilometers?
faq.a: The US and UK retained miles through historical inertia and political resistance to full metrication. The US Metric Conversion Act of 1975 made metrication voluntary, so road signage stayed in miles. Both countries use km in science and medicine. Metrication for road use has not been legislated.

faq.q: How accurate is this miles-to-km calculator?
faq.a: It uses the full exact factor **1.609344** (7 significant figures), not the rounded 1.6 or 1.61. Results are accurate for navigation, race timing, engineering, and sports science. The calculator also shows the round-trip distance automatically, useful for fuel and training planning.
